messages.content: 你能幫我找到紐約有閱讀室和小說區的公共圖書館，然後在洛杉磯有Wi-Fi和有兒童區的公共圖書館，最後在芝加哥有咖啡廳和閱讀室的公共圖書館嗎？

function.name: public_library_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby public libraries based on specific criteria like English fiction availability and Wi-Fi. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Boston, MA

facilities.description: Facilities and sections in public library.

The user wants to find libraries in three cities with certain facilities. We need to use the function public_library_find_nearby. We need to call it three times with appropriate parameters.

We need to produce calls to the function. The function signature: public_library_find_nearby({location: string, facilities: ...}). The facilities parameter can be one of the listed options: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[].

But the user wants multiple facilities per query. The function signature seems to allow only one facility? It says facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[]. That suggests that facilities can be a single string or an array of strings? Actually "Cafe"[] indicates an array of Cafe? Wait "Cafe"[] means array of "Cafe"? That seems odd. Maybe they want to pass an array of facilities. But the type says facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[]; So it's a union of string or array of "Cafe"? That seems wrong. But we can guess that we should pass an array of strings: ["Reading Room", "Fiction"] etc.

Thus we will call the function three times:

1. location: "New York, NY", facilities: ["Reading Room", "Fiction"]
2. location: "Los Angeles, CA", facilities: ["Wi-Fi", "Children Section"]
3. location: "Chicago, IL", facilities: ["Cafe", "Reading Room"]
